name: Approved run → project the change's tasks into immutable task.spec
description:
The projection station. The dev-from-task spec requires: WHEN run.change_approved is present for a run, THEN the change's tasks are projected as immutable task.spec facts (the dev loop converges on them, it does not redefine them). This rule is that trigger. It fires on the RUN entity after the human-approval gate releases (run.change_approved present, the run resumed to executing) and spawns a loop that calls the project_tasks tool, which reads the change's authored task facts off the run, enforces the Karpathy task schema, clamps each iteration budget to [1,5], binds to the VALIDATED content (D15 #0: it freezes only when openspec.validated equals openspec.change.<slug>.revision), and stamps the immutable task.spec.<i>.* package — or fails toward the human on a schema gap. G2: this rule fires no lifecycle transition; the projection is a tool writing evidence facts.

RUN BINDING: run_scope=inherit reads the run entity's bare agent.run triple (stamped by dev-from-task/01-anchor-run-for-dispatch, the same anchor the dev re-wake inherits) and sets the projection loop's RunID to it, so project_tasks resolves THIS run's entity from its tool-call metadata and stamps task.spec on it. A run entity carries no bare agent.run of its own, which is why 01 stamps the anchor first; this rule requires agent.run ne "" so it fires only once that anchor is present.

SLUG THREADING: project_tasks takes the change slug (the model says WHICH approved change to freeze). The run's change facts are slug-SCOPED (openspec.change.<slug>.*), so a rule cannot wildcard the slug out of the predicate key — create_change therefore also stamps a run-level slug pointer openspec.change.slug=<slug>, which this rule threads into the prompt via $entity.triple.openspec.change.slug. tool_choice=function forces the project_tasks call and tools stays nil (global discovery advertises project_tasks); the loop calls it and terminates (StopLoop), writing task.spec.* (not coordinator.decision.*), so it triggers no coordinator decision rule.

ROLE = coordinator (design roster: only Sarah/Amelia/Quinn; Sarah the coordinator owns the openspec/projection tools). There is no separate projector persona — this is a coordinator loop scoped to a tool, exactly like the create_change and validate_change authoring loops (coordinator/02, coordinator/03).

ORDERING (before the dev re-wake): the dev-loop kickoff re-wake (dev-from-task/02) is gated behind projection COMPLETION (it requires task.spec.0.test_command ne ""), so this projection runs first and the coordinator re-wakes only once task.spec exists — which its prompt assumes ('read the projected task specs'). This also serializes the two forced-tool turns so they do not race (the mock journey consumes tool turns against a positional cursor).

SELF-EXTINGUISHING ONE-SHOT (restart-safe): on_enter FIRST stamps the fired-once marker run.projection_kickoff=$entity.instance on the run, and the run.projection_kickoff length_eq 0 guard makes the trigger flip false the moment it fires. This is the house restart-safety pattern (semteams agent-run/02, and dev-from-task/02): publish_agent is NOT idempotent (each fire mints a fresh loop; the framework does not dedup), and the other trigger conditions (agent.run/executing/approved) stay true, so WITHOUT this marker a graph replay with no persisted rule-state (RULE_STATE wiped while ENTITY_STATES survives — asymmetric bucket loss) would re-spawn a DUPLICATE projection loop. The marker (a durable ENTITY_STATES triple) closes that independent of RULE_STATE. Marker stamped BEFORE the publish so a publish failure leaves the run stuck-toward-human rather than duplicated; project_tasks itself also refuses a second projection (task.spec is immutable), a second guard.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.coordinator
on_enter.prompt:
SEMDEV — the human approved this run's change and it resumed to executing. Project the change's tasks into the immutable task.spec facts the dev loop converges on.

Call project_tasks with the approved change slug: $entity.triple.openspec.change.slug. Emit only the slug — the harness reads the task definitions from the graph, enforces the task schema, and stamps task.spec. Calling project_tasks completes your turn.

metadata.station: project_tasks — freeze the approved change's tasks into immutable task.spec
metadata.trigger_rationale: spec: WHEN run.change_approved present THEN tasks projected. Fires on the RUN entity at approval, requiring the agent.run anchor (dev-from-task/01) so run_scope=inherit can bind the projection loop to this run.
metadata.role_rationale: coordinator (Sarah owns the projection tool; 3-role roster has no separate projector). tool_choice=function:project_tasks + nil tools (global discovery) forces the call — a tool turn, not a routing turn. Mirrors coordinator/02 create_change and coordinator/03 validate_change.
metadata.slug_threading: project_tasks needs the slug as a value; the run's change facts are slug-scoped so a rule cannot wildcard it. create_change stamps openspec.change.slug=<slug> (run-level pointer, its owned namespace) and this rule threads $entity.triple.openspec.change.slug.
metadata.ordering: runs BEFORE the dev re-wake (dev-from-task/02 is gated on task.spec.0.test_command ne ""), so the coordinator re-wakes only after task.spec exists and the two forced-tool turns do not race the journey's positional cursor.
metadata.restart_safe: SELF-EXTINGUISHING via the run.projection_kickoff marker + length_eq 0 guard (house pattern, semteams agent-run/02 / dev-from-task/02). publish_agent is not idempotent, so the one-shot is intrinsic (not reliant on durable RULE_STATE) — a duplicate projection loop cannot be spawned even under asymmetric RULE_STATE loss; project_tasks's task.spec immutability is a second guard.
metadata.deferred_rewake_scoping: like the other re-wakes, tools is omitted = global discovery; a real model could call a registered tool other than project_tasks. Inert under the mock (cursor). Closed with the coordinated MEDIUM-3 tool-scoping change (populate bootstrap allowed_tools + a scoped tools list on every spawn) before the first real-LLM token.
